entry.title: What LLM agent sessions hold while waiting on serverless and agent runtimes
entry.summary: Held While Waiting: What LLM Agent Sessions Reserve on Serverless and Agent Runtimes arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines how LLM agents occupy computing resources while waiting for model replies. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore as its main example, it finds that each conversation reserves a separate isolated environment until the conversation is closed, so environments run out long before processing power does. The authors propose closing environments promptly after conversations end and sharing one environment among many conversations, noting that sharing requires platform support. Keeping conversations separate without reserving an environment for each waiting conversation is presented as an open problem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors identify that LLM agent sessions hold dedicated environments while waiting on the model, and propose closing and sharing fixes, evaluated via a simulation and a benchmark.

entry.title: Optimal Preemption for Keeping Information Fresh in Mean Age and Beyond
entry.summary: Optimal Preemption: Guaranteeing Information Freshness in Mean Age and Beyond arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies Age of Information (AoI), where an update in service must normally wait even when heavy-tailed delays raise its age. The authors propose a framework in which the sender can preempt an in-service update and sample a fresh one, for general service-time distributions and explicit action costs. Under nondecreasing age costs, a finite mean delay is shown to suffice for finite average age even with infinite delay variance. For exponential service the optimal rule uses constant thresholds, while for general delays the optimal preemption rule depends on both the age and the elapsed service time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors allow preempting in-service updates and reduce VaR and CVaR minimization to the same optimality equations, validated under Pareto and log-normal delays.

entry.title: Self-orthogonal MDS codes from principal ideals
entry.summary: Self-Orthogonal MDS Principal-Ideal Codes arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies Euclidean self-orthogonality and the generalized Reed-Solomon (GRS) property for codes generated by a monic polynomial g and its shifts, with length r+k and dimension k, where 3≤k≤r. Over any algebraically closed field, the authors fully classify the generators that yield codes that are both self-orthogonal and GRS. For fixed r, k and characteristic, only finitely many such generators exist. When 3≤k<r, they show that each algebraically closed field supports infinitely many pairwise inequivalent, non-GRS self-orthogonal MDS codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete classification of self-orthogonal GRS generators over algebraically closed fields and prove infinitely many inequivalent non-GRS MDS codes, a strong theoretical result with

entry.title: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division of Chores
entry.summary: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division for Chores arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies fairly dividing indivisible chores that must be assigned in a fixed order, with the full list known in advance but assignments irreversible. The authors show that for three or more agents, some instances admit no allocation satisfying temporal envy-freeness up to one chore (TEF1), even up to any finite factor, and that deciding TEF1 existence is NP-complete. They also show that minimizing social cost under TEF1 cannot be approximated in polynomial time, but for a fixed number of agents they give an FPTAS for the optimal temporal EF1 factor with social cost guarantees. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question, showing TEF1 allocations may not exist for three or more agents, with NP-completeness and social-cost inapproximability results.

entry.title: Optimal impure quantum codes that recover erased qudits from few others
entry.summary: Optimal Impure (r,δ)-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes with Explicit Minimum Localities arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies quantum locally recoverable codes, where erased qudits can be recovered by accessing only a small number of other qudits. The authors build CSS codes from nested pairs of generalized monomial-Cartesian codes. They obtain four infinite families of GKT-optimal impure (r,δ)-qLRCs with disjoint recovering sets, and determine their minimum localities. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize minimum localities of CSS codes via local relative distances and construct four GKT-optimal impure quantum LRC families with determined minimum localities.

entry.title: Uniqueness, proximity, and scaling in atomic splittable polymatroid congestion games
entry.summary: Uniqueness, Proximity, and Scaling in Atomic Splittable Polymatroid Congestion Games arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a polynomial-time algorithm for computing exact equilibria in atomic splittable polymatroid congestion games with integral ranks and rational affine latencies. It first computes equilibria of integer-splittable versions of the game, then uses progressively finer packet sizes to recover the continuous equilibrium. The paper also proves that equilibria are unique for arbitrary real polymatroid ranks and convex, strictly increasing, continuously differentiable latencies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a polynomial-time exact equilibrium algorithm for atomic splittable polymatroid congestion games and prove uniqueness for arbitrary real ranks.

entry.title: Distortion in Online Voting: how well sequential elections approximate ideal choices
entry.summary: Distortion in Online Voting arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies distortion in online voting, a framework combining computational social choice with online algorithms. Unlike offline elections where all candidates are known in advance, here a fixed set of voters is present from the start while candidates arrive one at a time. Each arrival requires an immediate, irrevocable decision to keep the current candidate or switch. The authors give upper and lower bounds for deterministic and randomized mechanisms under utilitarian and metric preference frameworks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce online distortion for voting, giving deterministic and randomized bounds under utilitarian and metric preference models.

entry.title: Proportional representation for nearly solid coalitions and the proportional veto core for rankings
entry.summary: Proportional Representation for Almost-Solid Coalitions and the Proportional Veto Core for Rankings arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper extends proportional representation guarantees from candidate sets to rankings, introducing robust Rank-PSC and a stronger Rank-PSC+ axiom for almost-solid coalitions. It shows that such rankings can be constructed in polynomial time using reverse-sequential variants of Ordered Phragmén and STV. The authors also introduce Rank-Aligned PJR+ and examine how the Expanding Approvals Rule fares against these guarantees for fixed-size committees. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the proportional veto core to rankings, prove a tight bound on representation loss, and give polynomial-time constructions satisfying a stronger robust axiom.

entry.title: Thinflow: a small tool for keeping HPC benchmark campaigns rerunnable as directory trees
entry.summary: Thinflow: Organizing HPC Benchmarking Campaigns as Rerunnable Directory Trees arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents Thinflow, a small Bash engine that organizes high-performance computing benchmarking campaigns as rerunnable directory trees of tasks and runs. Each task is a directory with code and a short shell script, and one command builds the code, runs the benchmarks, and plots the results, with per-supercomputer profiles submitting jobs to Slurm. In a case study, the authors ran one campaign with identical task files on three Slurm partitions of two supercomputers, on up to 16 nodes, producing 455 benchmark runs.

entry.title: Distributed-memory parallel Star-M tensor SVD
entry.summary: StarMPI-SVD: Distributed-Memory Parallel Star-M Tensor SVD arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents the first distributed-memory parallel implementations of two Star-M tensor decompositions, t-SVDM-I and the adaptive multirank t-SVDM-II, generalized to N-way tensors. It uses asynchronous, non-blocking communication to speed up data redistribution and key computational kernels. Strong-scaling tests report at least 70% parallel efficiency on up to 128 nodes (6144 cores), and the methods are applied to application datasets up to 768 GB.

entry.title: Aggron: a serving system that aggressively compresses agent KV caches during request-queue stalls
entry.summary: Aggron: Aggressive Compression of Agentic KV Caches during Head-of-Line Stalls in the Request Queue arXiv · Nov 20, 2026LLM agents run long, multi-turn programs whose context grows each step, and their serving is limited by KV cache capacity. This paper presents Aggron, which summarizes agentic requests at every turn and selectively compresses only parts of the KV cache, while launching these summarizations from a separate Summarization Queue during head-of-line stalls in the main queue. Summarizations are issued only when the server predicts they will finish before the stalled request executes. In evaluation at high load, Aggron reduces P99 program latency by 27–31% and raises throughput by 1.34–1.40× compared with state-of-the-art asynchronous summarization.

entry.title: Faster Long-Context Attention via Dynamic Routing and KV-Centric GPU Execution
entry.summary: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents LightningMoBA, a method that speeds up Mixture of Block Attention (MoBA), which reduces long-context computation by selecting key-value blocks for each query. It replaces fixed Top-k selection with dynamic thresholding, groups work by KV block so that loaded tiles are reused, and overlaps memory transfers with Tensor Core computation on Hopper GPUs. At matched Top-16 retention across five checkpoints, end-to-end generation is 1.20 to 1.60 times faster, and mean RULER score rises from 74.42 to 75.28.

entry.title: Cooling noisy population protocols: averaging and localisation under persistent errors
entry.summary: Cooling Noisy Population Protocols -- Vanishing-Gain Averaging and Localisation under Persistent Errors arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how anonymous population protocols, where agents interact in random pairs, coordinate when communication and measurement errors persist. It proves that pairwise averaging with independent centred finite-variance communication errors converges with probability 1 to a common finite random value. For one-dimensional localisation, a signed update converges to the true agent locations up to one random translation, while a one-sided update fails to stabilise. The paper also shows that the signed protocol still converges when errors depend on inter-device distance.

entry.title: Spherical arrangement of circular antenna arrays for massive MIMO wireless systems
entry.summary: Spherical Tessellation of Circular Arrays for Massive MIMO: Favourable Propagation Conditions and Spectral Design arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies a concentric circular antenna array for upper-mid-band XL-MIMO, built by tessellating a sphere so that facet orientations are not separable. Under fixed normalised chord spacing and ideal facet visibility, the authors prove that user channels become asymptotically orthogonal and matched-filter SINR approaches the single-user SNR. Simulations confirm interference decay and SINR convergence. A spectral comparison shows that facet-normal diversity avoids the full-amplitude grating ridges of the cylindrical baseline, and the residual between facets decreases as the array grows.

entry.title: Toward Scale-Up Networks: Challenges and Open Questions
entry.summary: Towards Scale-Up Networking: Challenges and Open Questions arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper examines how communication between AI accelerators has become a key bottleneck in distributed training and inference. The authors analyze critical-path communication from parallelism strategies and derive requirements for domain scale, per-accelerator bandwidth, and collective completion latency. They use these requirements to compare representative proprietary and open scale-up fabrics. Based on this analysis and discussions with industry experts, the paper identifies open problems in physical interconnects and switching, efficient communication, semantics, resource sharing, and heterogeneous device interconnection.

entry.title: Live migration of streaming DeltaNet requests and the cost of log backlog
entry.summary: Live Migration of Gated DeltaNet Requests: Exact Catch-Up and the Cost of Log Backlog arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how to live-migrate a streaming Gated DeltaNet (GDN) request by recovering its recurrent state at the correct token boundary on a worker with the same model weights. It combines snapshots, batched replay, and token catch-up, and proposes a compact update-log migration path. In 1,350 pure-GDN trials on two GPU deployments, compact logs gave the shortest exact handoff gap in all 90 configurations, while exact catch-up always released the source earliest and 32-step replay gave the highest output rate when arithmetic differences were allowed.

entry.title: AscMLA: Faster long-context decoding using asymmetric FP4 scaling
entry.summary: AscMLA: Unlocking FP4 Efficiency for Long-Context MLA Decoding through Asymmetric Scaling arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents AscMLA, a method for speeding up long-context decoding that repeatedly reads a growing key-value cache. It combines asymmetric scaling for keys and values with pipelined scale delivery so a single FP4 data payload can be processed directly. The authors report 38.2% less cache memory than FP8 and geometric-mean speedups of 1.35x over TRT-LLM's FP8 kernels and 1.26x over CAKE's NVFP4 MLA kernels.

entry.title: Physics-informed deep learning for predicting channels in satellite metasurface reflection networks
entry.summary: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Channel Prediction in Satellite-Mounted Metasurface Reflection Communication Networks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework for predicting channels in satellite-mounted metasurface networks for 6G satellite-terrestrial communication. The framework embeds wireless physics, including monotonicity constraints and asymptotic decay, into a neural network to perform outage probability-aware prediction. The authors build a system model with spherical user distribution, a Spherical Poisson Point Process-based satellite constellation, and practical metasurface phase quantization. Simulations report prediction accuracy above 0.99 with physically consistent outage trends across geometries, constellation densities, and quantization resolutions.

entry.title: Two-timescale channel estimation and port selection for fluid antennas with few port observations
entry.summary: Two-Timescale Channel Estimation and Port Selection for Fluid Antenna Systems With Limited Port Observations arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Fluid antenna systems need instantaneous channel state information to select ports, but one RF chain can probe only a few ports per coherence block. The paper proposes a two-timescale scheme that exploits the slow variation of path angles, using a sequential Monte Carlo filter to accumulate the angle posterior across blocks while integrating out fast-fading path gains in closed form. Simulations show the scheme approaches selection with known angles after about twenty blocks, and with four probes per block matches memoryless schemes using eight.

entry.title: Asymptotic limits for codes under toroidal distance
entry.summary: Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies asymptotic bounds for codes in Z_q^n under the toroidal metric, where distances are measured modulo q. Using the classical Gilbert–Varshamov bounds for Hamming and Lee metrics as a baseline, it derives an asymptotic Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and a Hamming-type upper bound via a saddle-point approach. For 3 dividing q, it embeds ternary Hamming codes to obtain another lower bound. It also gives an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes and compares the bounds numerically.

entry.title: Sequential contract design for crowdsourcing under a fixed budget
entry.summary: Sequential Contract Design for Budgeted Crowdsourcing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how a principal can crowdsource tasks to workers under a fixed compensation budget, when workers' effort is unobservable. The principal offers contracts sequentially, using past outcomes and payments to choose whom to approach and what to offer, aiming to maximize expected work value without exceeding the budget. The authors characterize when polynomial-time constant-factor approximations are possible, depending on the numbers of workers, effort levels, and outcomes. They also examine simple contract rules and extend the analysis to monotone submodular valuations.

entry.title: Feedback-free FDD cell-free massive MIMO with sparse AP activation and dual-mode precoding
entry.summary: Feedback-Free FDD Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Sparse AP Activation and Dual-Mode Precoding arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes two mechanisms for practical frequency-division duplex operation in cell-free massive MIMO. Sparse access-point activation reduces downlink pilot overhead to enable coherent detection, while angle-reciprocity precoding steers beams using only uplink-estimated angles, removing channel feedback entirely. A load-adaptive optimizer chooses between closed-form signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio precoding for high load and semidefinite relaxation for low-load power minimization. Simulations show better spectral and energy efficiency than existing feedback-free FDD solutions and robustness to angle errors, reciprocity mismatch, and multipath.

entry.title: Choosing RISC-V Accelerators for Energy-Efficient Embedded Workloads
entry.summary: Matching Architecture to Workload: Comparing RISC-V Parallel Accelerators for Energy-Efficient Embedded Computing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper compares three execution models for energy-efficient embedded computing: scalar multicore, streaming multicore, and vector processing. It uses three open-source RISC-V accelerators, PULP Cluster, Snitch Cluster, and Spatz, implemented in the same 12 nm technology and evaluated with a common benchmark suite. The results show that no single model performs best across all workload classes. Spatz suits regular, highly vectorizable compute-intensive applications but is most sensitive to workload characteristics, while Snitch suits limited-parallelism, streamable workloads and PULP suits irregular, control-dominated ones. The flexibility of PULP and Snitch comes with a non-negligible cost in area and power compared with Spatz.

entry.title: Training channel estimators for fluid antennas from noisy pilots without full channel labels
entry.summary: Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses channel estimation for fluid antenna systems (FAS) using Fourier neural operators (FNOs). It proposes a self-supervised framework that trains the estimator directly from noisy, sub-sampled pilot observations, without labeled channel data, by combining pilot splitting with a Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) correction for noise bias. The authors prove the objective yields the same MMSE solution as ideal supervised training. Simulations report accuracy comparable to supervised training, zero-shot generalization to unseen port resolutions, and rapid recovery from distribution shift through online adaptation.

entry.title: A general method for building complex codebooks from functions on Abelian groups
entry.summary: A generic construction of complex codebooks from functions over Abelian groups arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper presents a generic construction and a modified construction of complex codebooks built from functions on finite Abelian groups. Codebooks with small inner-product correlation improve performance in areas such as direct spread code division multiple access, space-time coding, and compressed sensing. By choosing perfect nonlinear functions, the authors systematically obtain several families of codebooks that are optimal or asymptotically optimal with respect to the Welch or Levenshtein bounds. The constructions recover several known optimal codebooks and also yield new codebooks with previously unreported parameters.

entry.title: Intent-Defined Radio: a goal-driven design for future wireless networks
entry.summary: Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proposes Intent-Defined Radio (IDR), a new system abstraction that links explicit service goals, such as latency and reliability, to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space, using large language models. The authors present two simulation studies with Intent2MAC showing executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. Replacing random contention with distributed urgency-based arbitration improved service satisfaction and remote-control performance, at a cost in throughput. The paper also discusses open challenges and outlines a staged path toward deployment.

entry.title: CheckCo: a checkpoint-based method for balancing uneven event streams across workers
entry.summary: CheckCo: Checkpoint-Coordinated Load Balancing for Skewed Event Streams at Scale arXiv · Nov 17, 2026In event streams, a few heavy keys can generate far more events than others, overloading some workers. CheckCo is a load-balancing algorithm that estimates per-key frequencies from the live stream without prior statistics. At each checkpoint, it merges the counts into a partitioning function that splits keys in proportion to their estimated frequency and assigns them to workers. On a production pipeline handling over 100 billion events per day, the most loaded worker received 9.8% more events than the daily average.

entry.title: A nonadaptive method for finding the main frequency components of signals in any dimension
entry.summary: A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies the sparse Fourier transform over the group (Z/2^aZ)^d, where the signal is accessed through point queries. It presents a randomized algorithm that uses non-adaptive queries to output a k-sparse estimate, with error bounded by an absolute constant times the best k-sparse approximation error, with high probability. The constant can be made arbitrarily close to 1 under extra conditions, and the method extends to (Z/b^aZ)^d for any integer b>1. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a nonadaptive sparse Fourier transform over (Z/2^aZ)^d with l2 error constant C improvable to 1+epsilon, plus sample and operation bounds in every dimension.

entry.title: Sharper constants for Kautz-Singleton group testing designs
entry.summary: Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies probabilistic nonadaptive group testing, where a random set of d defective items among N is identified using a binary test matrix. It revisits the explicit Kautz-Singleton construction and improves the leading constant in the test count for the COMP decoder, and shows the DD decoder meets the same bound. Both decoders are shown to have vanishing average error probability with at most (1/ln 2+ε)d log N tests under stated conditions.

entry.title: Generalized covering radii and deep holes of antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH codes in even characteristic
entry.summary: Generalized Covering radii and Deep Holes of a Family of Antiprimitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes in Even Characteristic arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies a family of antiprimitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length q+1 and designed distance 3 over F_q, where q=2^m and m≥2. It establishes the generalized covering-radius hierarchy: the covering radius is 3, and the t-th generalized covering radius is 4 for every t≥2. The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a received word to be a deep hole and provides an explicit parametrization of all deep-hole coset representatives.

entry.title: TripleKV: A three-tier KV cache system that prefetches agent cache data before it is needed
entry.summary: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect -- KV Cache Management for AI Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses the problem that AI agents, which alternate between model inference and tool calls, accumulate key-value (KV) caches too large for GPU memory under high concurrency. TripleKV predicts when tool calls will finish using a tool-aware latency predictor and prefetches the needed KV blocks from SSD into host DRAM in advance. It also removes duplicate blocks between GPU and DRAM and refills evicted GPU blocks from SSD through a victim-cache mechanism. The reported results show that the share of requests needing critical-path SSD reads falls from 45–76% to under 10%, and P95 time to first token drops by up to 49%.

entry.title: Structure and Complexity of Perfect Functional Representations: whether a variable Z can capture all information about Y not contained in X
entry.summary: Structure and Complexity of Perfect Functional Representations arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies functional representations in which Y equals g(X,Z) for a deterministic function g and a random variable Z independent of X, with Z perfectly capturing the information about Y not in X, meaning I(Y;Z)=H(Y|X). The authors give a necessary and sufficient condition for a conditional distribution p(Y|X) to admit such a perfect representation and cast checking this as a linear program. They also present an algorithm polynomial in |Y| and exponential in |X|, and prove that the decision problem is NP-complete for rational input matrices in binary encoding.

entry.title: Berth: GPU sharing that keeps latency SLOs without new preemption
entry.summary: Berth: SLO-Preserving GPU Sharing Without New Preemption arXiv · Nov 19, 2026Inference services reserve GPUs for worst-case load, leaving much capacity idle, but sharing with best-effort work usually breaks latency targets. Berth is a user-space system that uses the GPU's built-in time-slicer, feeding best-effort work through a preloaded shim only when no request needs the GPU. It also handles continuous-batching LLM engines and shortens the best-effort time slice, without changing applications, frameworks, kernels, or drivers. Across 31 scenarios and 13 baselines, Berth meets SLOs close to running alone and delivers 2.7 to 3.5 times the best-effort throughput of the strongest baselines.

entry.title: Twindex: index-cache offloading with coarse-to-fine selection for long-context sparse-attention serving
entry.summary: Twindex: Index Cache Offloading with Coarse-to-Fine Selection for Long-Context Sparse-Attention Serving arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses the GPU memory limit on concurrent requests when decoding long contexts with sparse-attention models, where the indexer cache becomes the bottleneck once the main KV cache is moved to host memory. The authors propose Twindex, which keeps a compact copy of the indexer cache in GPU memory and the full cache in host memory, using the copy to select candidates that the model's own indexer then narrows to top-k. Reported results at 1M tokens show roughly 1.6 to 3 times more requests fitting than KV offloading alone, up to about 2.5 times decode throughput, and mean benchmark scores at most 3.1% below the baseline.

entry.title: No binary linear [65,9,29] code exists
entry.summary: There is no binary linear [65,9,29] code arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper proves that no binary linear [65,9] code with minimum distance at least 29 exists, equivalently that no even binary linear [66,9] code with minimum distance at least 30 exists. Combined with known constructions, it determines d_2(65,9)=28, n_2(9,29)=66 and n_2(9,30)=67, and it also gives d_2(122,10)=56. The nonexistence proof associates a quadratic function with a hypothetical even code and analyzes it using character sums, weight moments and the exclusion of weight-42 codewords.

entry.title: Thirteen Improved Binary Constant-Weight Codes with Verifiable Cyclic Orbit Certificates
entry.summary: Thirteen Improved Binary Constant-Weight Codes with Explicit Cyclic Orbit Certificates arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents thirteen explicit binary constant-weight codes that improve lower bounds listed in Brouwer's table, such as A(29,6,5)≥333, A(55,4,5)≥66144, and A(62,4,5)≥107360. The codes contain 408,729 codewords, specified by 11,386 orbit representatives under given cyclic coordinate permutations. A standalone reconstruction and distance verifier is provided, and all thirteen orbit expansions were confirmed to match the full codeword lists.

entry.title: Sharp Complexity Thresholds for Network Cournot Competition (how hard it is to compute equilibria in networked firm markets)
entry.summary: Sharp Complexity Thresholds for Network Cournot Competition arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper determines how hard it is to approximate network Cournot equilibria, depending on demand polynomial degree and the number of firms per market. Cubic demands are polynomial-time solvable at high precision for any market size, while quartic and quintic demands remain tractable with at most three and two firms per market. Beyond these thresholds, approximation is shown to be PPAD-hard. The paper also gives a polynomial-time algorithm for arbitrary-degree nonincreasing concave polynomial demands when each firm's cost depends only on its total production. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report exact complexity thresholds for network Cournot equilibrium approximation, tied to demand degree and firms per market, with PPAD-hardness and a polynomial-time algorithm.

entry.title: Optimal online auction competitive ratio for subadditive valuations is below 1/2
entry.summary: The Optimal Competitive Ratio for Subadditive Online Combinatorial Auctions is Less Than 1/2 arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper builds a four-buyer online combinatorial auction with independent subadditive valuations and a fixed, known arrival order. In this instance, every online rule earns strictly less than half the expected offline optimum. The paper computes the optimal online and offline welfare exactly and shows that a 1/2 guarantee always holds with at most three buyers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a four-buyer subadditive online combinatorial auction counterexample showing the optimal competitive ratio is below 1/2, contrasting with a 1/2 guarantee for three buyers.

entry.title: Capacity of a random-bag communication channel with and without feedback
entry.summary: The Asymptotic Capacity of the Grabbag Channel With and Without Feedback arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies communication through a randomly mixed store called the Grabbag channel. Each use inserts a ball of one of K colors into a bag of M balls, then one of the resulting M+1 balls is chosen uniformly, observed, and removed. The authors show that for 2 ≤ K ≤ M+1, both the no-feedback capacity and the capacity with noiseless strictly causal output feedback are at most 9.77(K/(M+1))^{2/3}. For M+1 ≥ 2^22 both are at least an absolute constant times (K/(M+1))^{2/3}, so both are of order (K/M)^{2/3}. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give matching-order bounds of (K/(M+1))^{2/3} on the capacity with and without feedback, with proofs for both directions.

entry.title: Analyzing an Unexplored SASS Control-Code Field: Barrier Exemption and Programmable Warp Priority
entry.summary: Dissecting an Unexplored SASS Control-Code Field: Barrier Exemption and Programmable Warp Priority arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a previously unexplored control-code field in NVIDIA's native GPU instruction set (SASS), which appears frequently in closed-source libraries such as cuBLAS and cuDNN but is never emitted by nvcc for user programs. Using instruction-level microbenchmarks across GPU architectures from Volta to Blackwell, the authors show the field controls two hardware mechanisms: barrier exemption (EXEMPT) and programmable warp priority (START, TILE, END). They also implement a post-compilation binary optimizer that inserts these marks without changing source code or the compiler, achieving speedups of up to 31.9% on representative kernels across six GPUs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically study an unexplored SASS control-code field, identifying barrier exemption and warp priority mechanisms, and report speedups on six GPUs and in llama.cpp and vLLM.

entry.title: Mining Temporal Rules Locally and Verifying Them Globally in Distributed Monitoring
entry.summary: Mine Locally, Verify Globally: Exact Recovery, Compilation, and Distortion of Mined Temporal Rules arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies how temporal rules mined from system traces can be applied in distributed monitoring, where observations come from nodes with unsynchronized clocks. The authors compare local mining followed by global confirmation with centralized trace merging in terms of rule coverage, and examine when temporal windows are needed and how event loss affects detection. The evaluation uses IPv6 packet traces collected from 21 receivers across four continents. The results show that local mining with global confirmation can recover centralized coverage under suitable conditions while reducing communication overhead, whereas merging traces with unaligned clocks can distort coverage.

entry.title: On cyclic codes built from cyclotomic polynomials
entry.summary: On cyclic codes generated by cyclotomic polynomials arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies cyclic codes over finite fields generated by cyclotomic polynomials, extending recent work by Bhagat and Sarma. It determines the exact minimum distances of these codes and of their dual codes. The authors show that all four code families are linear complementary dual and locally recoverable, and identify several infinite families that are optimal with respect to the Singleton-type bound for such codes.

entry.title: Relative Entropy Bounds Under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints
entry.summary: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Exact Bounds and Extremizers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper derives a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy D(P‖Q) in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences χ²(P‖Q) and χ²(Q‖P). Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions attain both bounds simultaneously. Consequently, if one chi-squared divergence tends to zero while the other stays uniformly bounded, both relative entropies tend to zero. Under exact constraints, the infimum of D(P‖Q) is zero and is not attained on alphabets with at least three elements.

entry.title: How the hull dimension of algebraic geometry codes changes under divisor twists
entry.summary: Hull variation of algebraic geometry codes under divisor twists arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies how the hull (the intersection of a linear code with its dual) changes when a code is rescaled, focusing on algebraic geometry codes over function fields. It gives a formula and an upper bound for the change in hull dimension and builds explicit twists that raise or lower the hull dimension step by step. These are applied to two classical code families. Starting from known LCD codes, the authors reach a range of hull dimensions, and starting from self-dual or maximal-hull codes, they reach zero, producing LCD codes of various dimensions.

entry.title: A runtime system that reduces crossbar port contention on SM-partitioned GPUs
entry.summary: A Runtime System for Mitigating Crossbar Port Contention on SM-Partitioned GPUs arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper explains that even with SM partitioning such as CUDA Green Contexts, concurrent workloads can slow down latency-critical ones, partly because all SMs in a GPC share one crossbar port to the L2 cache. The authors present GPCPlace, a runtime that profiles workloads on the target GPU to choose between spreading and packing them across GPCs, setting SM masks by hooking kernel launches in the CUDA driver without application changes. Across 14 GPUs and 112 workload cases, it reports average speedups of up to 1.15x and a maximum of 2.38x for latency-critical workloads over Green Contexts, without throughput loss.

entry.title: Ordinal Hegselmann-Krause Systems: Opinion Dynamics Using Median-Style Aggregation
entry.summary: Ordinal Hegselmann-Krause Systems arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a variant of the Hegselmann-Krause opinion model in which agents update opinions using median or other ordinal aggregation methods instead of averages. It analyzes convergence under synchronous and asynchronous update schedules. Under a 1-Lipschitz condition, asynchronous dynamics converge in worst-case time O(n^4), with sharper bounds for median and k-large aggregation, while synchronous dynamics converge in linear time. When the Lipschitz condition is violated, synchronous dynamics may fail to converge at all.

entry.title: Rational vs. Radical: How Repeated Bayesian Updates Drift
entry.summary: Rational v. Radical: Trajectory Properties of Iterated Bayesian Updates arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies what happens when Jeffrey's update is applied repeatedly to fixed evidence, which under suitable conditions yields a maximum-likelihood estimate. Running the iteration in reverse corresponds to repeated prior hacking, and most interior priors are shown to approach certainty in one possibility, a behavior the authors call radicalization. The work also asks whether some evidence can drive every interior prior to the same conclusion.

entry.title: ScaleBench: A Reproducible Platform for Testing Kubernetes Autoscaling
entry.summary: ScaleBench: An Extensible and Reproducible Experimental Platform for Kubernetes Autoscaling Research arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents ScaleBench, an experimental platform that runs natively on Kubernetes for evaluating autoscaling solutions in a reproducible and extensible way. Unlike existing approaches, it integrates autoscalers as native Kubernetes components, so researchers can assess deployment characteristics and integration requirements alongside scaling performance. The authors demonstrate the platform through a case study evaluating several autoscaling approaches. The results show it supports systematic, repeatable, and practical assessment of Kubernetes autoscaling.

entry.title: Dividing Large Graphs Across Many GPUs in Supercomputers
entry.summary: Multilevel Graph Partitioning on GPU Supercomputers arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a new partitioner that splits large graphs across multiple GPUs in distributed supercomputers. It builds on Jet, an earlier single-GPU partitioner, and uses CUDA-aware MPI, one-sided communication, and a bulk-synchronous parallel design. The authors report solution quality comparable to Jet and good weak scaling up to 256 GPUs, allowing much larger instances than a single GPU can handle.

entry.title: Unified framework for super-resolution direction-of-arrival estimation in antenna arrays
entry.summary: DOA Estimation in Antenna Arrays: Super-Resolution Methods in a Common Space arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for angular super-resolution in antenna arrays, combining linear prediction beyond the physical aperture, entropy variations, and harmonic spatial spectra averaging. It recasts classical methods such as Capon, Pisarenko, Maximum Entropy, and MUSIC into a single structure. The framework is extended to ESPRIT-type methods and adapted to non-Gaussian signals for Virtual-ESPRIT-type methods. It also proposes J-orthogonalization-based algorithms that produce spatial spectrum estimates for multiple super-resolution methods within one computational architecture.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination: a study of the running time of a fair-division algorithm
entry.summary: On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper examines the envy cycle elimination (ECE) algorithm, a basic method for fairly dividing indivisible goods. The algorithm guarantees an allocation that is envy-free up to one good under arbitrary monotone utilities. The authors show it can be implemented in O(nm) time for n agents and m goods, and that this bound is tight.

entry.title: eFAIR: Fair LLM serving under hourly electricity commitments
entry.summary: eFAIR: Fair LLM Serving under Hourly Electricity Commitments arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how datacenters serving large language models can allocate electricity bought hour by hour in day-ahead markets while treating requests fairly. The authors define normalized throughput and formulate fair serving as leximin optimization under an hourly electricity constraint. They present eFAIR, an online scheduler that coordinates request dispatching, electricity budget allocation, and GPU frequency selection. On H20 and H200 configurations with 32 replicas each, eFAIR raises the tenth percentile of normalized throughput by 28.0%-31.0% over the best budget-feasible baseline, with deviations from the hourly commitment below 0.26%.

entry.title: Rings Where a Linear Map, Its Inverse, and Transpose Share Information Exchange
entry.summary: A Characterization of Rings Where a Linear Transformation and Its Inverse and Transpose Have the Same Information Exchange arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper studies linear transformations over finite commutative rings. It shows that an invertible linear transformation and its inverse have equal information exchange over any ring. It also proves that a linear transformation and its transpose have equal information exchange if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications to the Discrete Fourier Transform, Vandermonde transformations, and area-time complexity are presented.

entry.title: Ternary minimal linear codes of dimension n+r built from index codes, with access structures of their duals
entry.summary: Construction of Ternary Minimal Linear Codes with Dimension n+r Via Index Codes and The Access Structures of Their Dual Codes arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proposes a general method for constructing ternary linear codes of dimension n+r and gives a necessary and sufficient condition for these codes to be minimal. Specific instances use index codes arising from spreads and from Krawtchouk polynomials, yielding several families of minimal codes with computed parameters and weight enumerators. The access structures of the secret-sharing schemes based on the dual codes are also determined. Several of the constructed families violate the Ashikhmin-Barg condition.

entry.title: MIMO channel extrapolation to unmeasured radiation modes via learned path correction
entry.summary: MIMO Channel Extrapolation to Unobserved Radiation Modes via Learned Path Refinement arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper addresses pattern-reconfigurable MIMO receivers, where sampling every antenna element still leaves some radiation modes unobserved. The authors propose a learned estimator that corrects the complex gains and spatial frequencies of shared propagation paths, so a correction inferred from measured rows updates all modes. Trained on complete simulated channels, the method reduces prediction error on wholly unobserved modes as well as across the full channel.

entry.title: Locality-aware scheduling for stream processing in serverless systems
entry.summary: Locality-Aware Scheduling for Stream Processing Applications in Serverless Environments arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper addresses stream processing applications running in stateful serverless environments, where pipelines are built from chained function invocations. It proposes LcSched, a distributed scheduling strategy that maximises local execution of chained invocations and ensures each execution accesses its state from the local worker. LcSched also monitors runtime workload to keep load balanced across workers. Experiments show throughput improvements of up to 3.6x and end-to-end latency reductions of up to 79% compared with the state-of-the-art distributed scheduling strategy.

entry.title: FlatCake: A flat storage design for reusing LLM attention caches across host memory and SSD
entry.summary: A Flat KV Cache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving arXiv · Oct 28, 2026FlatCake is a storage architecture for LLM serving that treats host DRAM and NVMe SSD as equal peer media in one unified address space, instead of a tiered cache. Each KV block is placed at creation directly on its target medium in session-contiguous, layer-major order and is never moved. On a production Claude Code trace, the authors report a 94% cache hit rate under increasing load (versus 64% for Mooncake) and a 1.6× reduction in peak-load mean TTFT.

entry.title: Fair Splitting of Goods and Chores Over Time
entry.summary: Temporal Fair Division: Simultaneous Guarantees for Goods and Chores arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies fair division of indivisible goods and chores when items arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably. For goods, it gives a polynomial-time algorithm that simultaneously achieves exact temporal proportionality up to one item, a 1/n approximation to temporal maximin share, and a 1/(n-1) approximation to temporal envy-freeness up to one item. For chores, it gives an algorithm achieving exact TPROP1 and a 2-1/n approximation to temporal maximin share, and shows this factor is optimal under that constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors study temporal fair division of indivisible goods and chores, reporting polynomial-time algorithms that simultaneously achieve TPROP1, TMMS and TEF1 approximations, plus tight-bound and im

entry.title: Stephen: Verifying Sequencer-Aided Coordination Systems with Cross-View Prophecy
entry.summary: Stephen: Verifying Sequencer-Aided Coordination Systems with Cross-View Prophecy arXiv · Nov 18, 2026Many distributed systems use dedicated sequencers to order requests, with replicas committing them in that order. This paper presents Stephen, a framework that extends prophecy variables across view changes so a proof can follow each request until it is committed or permanently discarded. The authors found and fixed bugs in existing implementations, including one that could lose committed requests. Applied to NOPaxos, Corfu and LazyLog, the framework yields verified implementations with machine-checked linearizability proofs that perform within 17% of unverified open-source versions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose cross-view prophecy variables for sequencer view changes, find and fix a bug losing committed requests, and report machine-checked linearizability proofs for NOPaxos, Corfu, and La

entry.title: SFiD: A self-supervised method for optimizing next-generation wireless networks
entry.summary: SFiD: Self-Supervised Fitness-Driven Optimization for Next-Generation Networking arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper introduces SFiD, a self-supervised fitness-driven diffusion method that generates its own training data and learns from it iteratively to solve complex optimization problems in next-generation wireless networks. The authors validate its convergence to the global optimum on analytical convex and non-convex problems. They apply continuous and discrete variants, plus a binary neural network version, to optimize RIS phase shifts in cell-free massive MIMO systems. Experiments report improved computational efficiency and performance comparable to or better than meta-heuristic and deep reinforcement learning benchmarks.

entry.title: Benchmark of traditional and learning-based reference-free compressors for long-read sequencing data
entry.summary: Benchmarking Traditional and Learning-Based Reference-Free Compressors for Long-Read Sequencing Data arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents LRCBench, a benchmark and survey of reference-free lossless compressors for long-read sequencing data. The authors review traditional and learning-based general-purpose and sequencing-specific methods, then evaluate 35 compressors on 16 real-world datasets from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio platforms. They compare compression ratio, storage savings, runtime, peak memory, and robustness, with learning-based methods tested on six MinION datasets. CoLoRd achieves the best overall compression ratios, while other methods offer different trade-offs in speed, memory use, and robustness.

entry.title: Spatial sampling design for reconfigurable MIMO channel extrapolation
entry.summary: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies how distributing radiation modes across antenna elements in pattern-reconfigurable arrays affects the reconstruction of unmeasured channels. The authors analyze how this spatial assignment enters the inverse problem and show that aperture-based layouts can fail to capture path correlations in multipath propagation. Simulations compare balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling, finding that balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error when some modes are unobserved.

entry.title: Drift-aware adaptive update strategy for semantic codecs in dynamic communication systems
entry.summary: Drift-Aware Adaptive Semantic Codec Update Strategy for Dynamic Semantic Communications arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper addresses how distribution drift makes offline-trained semantic codec models stale in dynamic semantic communication systems. It quantifies drift intensity in the semantic feature space and introduces Drift-Aware Age of Model (DA-AoM), which jointly captures drift-induced performance degradation, drift-dependent update service delay, and conventional update latency. Closed-form average DA-AoM expressions are derived for edge-layer M/M/1 and cloud-layer D/M/1 scenarios, and the update frequency is optimized under a queueing-stability constraint. Simulations show the strategy reduces average DA-AoM by 9.2% to 42.4% compared with representative baselines under the same resource constraints.

entry.title: Extending and testing when safe Pareto improvements are possible in games
entry.summary: Expanding and Evaluating the Applicability of Safe Pareto Improvements arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies safe Pareto improvements (SPIs), where players make commitments that create a new game isomorphic to the original after removing strictly dominated actions, yet Pareto better in every entry. The authors build token games, cheap-talk games made meaningful by commitments tied to token outcomes. They analyze SPIs under three added abilities: burning utility, transferring utility between players, and transferring utility with an outside party conditional on the token outcome. The paper also evaluates frameworks by how often SPIs arise in random games, reporting substantially better results than prior work.

entry.title: DexAttention: Distributed Sparse Attention with Fast Online Planning and Persistent GPU Execution
entry.summary: DexAttention: Distributed Sparse Attention through Rapid Online Planning and Persistent GPU Execution arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper presents DexAttention, a distributed sparse attention system that combines fast online planning with persistent GPU execution. Its assigner uses GPU-accelerated, topology-aware clustering to balance computation and reduce communication, while a greedy scheduler orders coarse operations and a persistent kernel on each GPU handles fine-grained dependencies. On a four-node, 16-GPU cluster, it reports a 1.39x geometric-mean end-to-end training speedup over the fastest applicable baseline across 11 configurations. For dynamic video attention, it reports 2.11 to 2.37x speedups over Ring Attention, including planning time.

entry.title: Electromagnetic channel model for integrated sensing and communication with one cylindrical target
entry.summary: Electromagnetic Channel Model and Sensing Performance for ISAC: The Case of a Single Cylindrical Scatterer arXiv · Nov 18, 2026The paper proposes an electromagnetic wireless channel model for accurate target localization in radar-like sensing. It is built on wave scattering theory with boundary conditions and models the target as a single cylindrical scatterer, yielding a channel transfer matrix valid in both near and far fields. Localization accuracy is evaluated with the Cramér-Rao lower bound for dielectric cylinders with varying position, radius, and dielectric constant.

entry.title: Model Discovery for Virtual Chaos Engineering with Incomplete Tracing: An eBPF Study
entry.summary: Model Discovery for Virtual Chaos Engineering with Incomplete Tracing: An eBPF Study arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper examines how to build executable operation models for virtual fault experiments in legacy systems that lack complete tracing, using external observations collected with eBPF. The authors ran a 108-case study across three public applications, varying SDK tracing from absent to full, and compared model forecasts with independent execution checks. With SDK tracing disabled, the tested OpenTelemetry eBPF path supported all seven operations in two applications, and the paper identifies the conditions and limits of this acquisition route.

entry.title: Computational hardness of online stochastic matching under random arrivals
entry.summary: Computational Hardness of Online Stochastic Matching arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies online stochastic matching on bipartite graphs, where offline vertices are known in advance and online requests arrive from known distributions, each being matched immediately and irrevocably or rejected. It gives the first computational hardness results for random-order arrivals. For known i.i.d. arrivals, computing the online optimum is APX-hard, so no polynomial-time approximation scheme exists unless P = NP. For random-order arrivals with only one offline node, computing the optimal online policy is #P-hard. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first hardness results for random-order online stochastic matching, claiming APX-hardness for i.i.d. arrivals and #P-hardness in the prophet secretary setting.

entry.title: A shared exponential lower bound for Dantzig and modified simplex in deterministic discounted games
entry.summary: A Common Exponential Lower Bound for Dantzig and Modified Simplex in Deterministic Discounted Games arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies a family of N-state deterministic two-player discounted games in which runs alternate adaptively between Dantzig's rule and the modified simplex method. It shows that, regardless of tie breaking, such runs from a specified initial strategy need 2^{Ω(N)} switches. The paper also presents a return-gate construction with related results, and shows Dantzig's rule is strongly polynomial under certain structural conditions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a shared exponential lower bound for Dantzig and modified simplex on deterministic discounted games, with a return-gate construction and polynomial-time sufficient conditions.

entry.title: Computational hardness of the covering radius for sparse LDPC parity-check codes
entry.summary: Hardness and Inapproximability of the Covering Radius for LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the covering-radius decision problem for sparse binary parity-check matrices with bounded row and column weights, asking whether every syndrome can be produced by an error vector of Hamming weight at most r. It proves the problem is Π₂ᴾ-complete when the maximum row and column weights are three, and remains Π₂ᴾ-hard under a constant multiplicative gap. The authors also derive an explicit NP-hard approximation factor under the same weight constraints, starting from Vertex Cover on 3-regular graphs. They note that if either maximum weight is at most two, the covering radius is computable in polynomial time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show covering-radius decision for LDPC codes is Π2P-complete at weight three, with a constant gap and a sharp weight-threshold result, mainly impacting coding-theory complexity.

entry.title: Resolving the Computational and Structural Complexity of Bertrand Networks
entry.summary: Settling the Time and Structural Complexity of Bertrand Networks arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the Bertrand network game of Babaioff et al. (2013), in which sellers must post a single price across captive and shared markets. It proves that computing a constant-error approximate Nash equilibrium in general Bertrand networks is PPAD-complete, even on sparse bipartite graphs of maximum degree five. It also gives an efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme when the maximum degree and the number of sellers with captive buyers are bounded. Finally, it shows every achievable equilibrium revenue profile can be realized with structural complexity O(2^n), and this bound is tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open problem on Bertrand network equilibria, proving PPAD-completeness for general graphs and a tight 2^O(n) structural complexity bound.

entry.title: Equilibrium Statistics and Stability in Random Two- and Three-Population Evolutionary Games
entry.summary: Equilibrium Statistics and Stability in Random Two-Population and Three-Population Evolutionary Games arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper studies evolutionary games with two or three populations, each having two strategies, when payoffs are uncertain but fixed along each trajectory. For two populations, it derives probabilities of equilibrium existence and analytical stability results for generic games and for diversity, exclusive, and avoidance games. For three populations, it gives existence probabilities for every equilibrium type and joint existence-and-stability probabilities for boundary equilibria. Monte Carlo simulations support these results and show that, under the same Gaussian sampling, three populations yield fully mixed equilibria less often but multistability more often than two.

entry.title: SPICE: sparse parameter gossip method for efficient LLM pretraining
entry.summary: SPICE: Sparse Parameter Gossip for LLM Pretraining arXiv · Nov 18, 2026SPICE is a communication-efficient method for pretraining large language models across geographically distributed resources with limited internet bandwidth. It combines sparse parameter gossip, where peers exchange only sparse corrected parameter values, with error feedback. Compared with the evaluated dense decentralized baselines, it achieves better training quality with less communication and higher throughput under bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: blaris: Windowless Random-Access LZSS Decompressor for Tiny Microcontrollers
entry.summary: blaris: Windowless Random-Access LZSS for Constrained Microcontrollers arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper presents blaris, a lightweight LZSS decompressor for constrained microcontrollers that supports random access during execute-in-place operation. It partitions tokens into bidirectionally traversable streams with power-of-two checkpoints, so back-references are resolved within the compressed payload without allocating a RAM sliding window. On RV32IMC it uses 548-784 bytes of Flash and 104-112 bytes of RAM, and it reports much faster small-slice random reads than ratio-matched, block-indexed heatshrink and tamp.

entry.title: Client-side reordering of data blocks to improve server-side compression in distributed file systems
entry.summary: Similarity-Aware Client-Side Reordering for Server-Side Storage Compression in Distributed File Systems arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes a client-side framework that reorders physical block layout before data is persisted, so that similar blocks share the same compression scope. It works with existing storage-server compressors without replacing them. Implemented in the SkyFS distributed file system with Zstandard on OpenZFS, it reduces physical storage by up to 42.9% compared with logical-order writes. Sequential-read throughput and random-read IOPS remain at 94-108% and 91-99% of baseline, respectively.

entry.title: Decentralized equilibrium learning in aggregate-reward Markov games, applied to smart grids
entry.summary: Exploiting Aggregate Feedback for Decentralized Equilibrium Learning in Markov Games: A Smart Grid Application arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies Markov games in which each agent's payoff depends on its own action and an aggregate of others' actions. It proposes a stage-based V-learning algorithm that combines aggregate-based prediction with hybrid-feedback Exp3-IX, requiring no opponent information or transition kernel knowledge. The authors prove a high-probability regret bound tied to aggregate prediction errors and show the method learns approximate coarse correlated equilibria. In a microgrid with prosumers and shared storage, it yields smaller deviation gaps than three learning baselines.

entry.title: Byzantine-tolerant robot gathering under round-robin scheduling
entry.summary: Byzantine Resilience of Robot Gathering under Round-Robin Scheduling arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies deterministic gathering of n anonymous, oblivious mobile robots in the plane under round-robin scheduling with rigid movement, when f Byzantine robots are present. The goal is for all correct robots to gather at one point in finite time and remain there forever. The authors analyze ToMax, a simple algorithm in which robots move to a point of maximum multiplicity and stay still only if their position is the unique maximum. They prove ToMax achieves gathering whenever f is at most floor(sqrt(n)/2), establishing an Ω(sqrt(n)) lower bound on achievable Byzantine resilience.

entry.title: Building reversible linear and DNA codes from T_{D,g}^n-sets and right polycyclic codes
entry.summary: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through T_D,gⁿ⁻set and (n₁,c₁|n₂,c₂₎₋right polycyclic codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents a method for constructing T_{D,g}^n-sets for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes, yielding many reversible MDS codes with improved parameters over an earlier construction. It gives concatenation-based constructions of reversible linear codes that are self-dual or linear complementary dual (LCD), with necessary and sufficient conditions for these properties. It also introduces (n1,c1|n2,c2)-right polycyclic codes and a construction of reversible MDS codes of this type over any finite commutative ring.

entry.title: FAST: A Method for Quickest Change Detection with Adaptive Sensing of Functional Data
entry.summary: FAST: Functional Adaptive Sensing and Testing for Quickest Change Detection arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies quickest change detection for functional data streams that are only partially observed, with each function measured at a fixed number of locations. After an unknown change point, the function's mean shifts, and this shift is assumed to have a sparse representation in a localized basis. The authors propose FAST, which jointly estimates the post-change parameter, chooses sensing locations, and performs sequential detection. The paper provides a minimax lower bound on worst-case detection delay under an average-run-length constraint, and a non-asymptotic estimation-error bound for adaptively sensed observations. Simulations and a wildfire case study are used to demonstrate performance.

entry.title: Kissing number of Craig's lattices and list decoding of spherical codes
entry.summary: On the Kissing Number of Craig's Lattice and Spherical List Decoding arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies Craig's lattices A_{p-1}^k, which have large kissing numbers relative to their dimension. The authors give a polynomial-time list decoder for spherical codes built from these lattices, for angular distance below 45 degrees. They show that Bacher's lower bound on the kissing number is asymptotically tight for k = o(log p / log log p), and they present an efficient algorithm used to compute kissing numbers in dimensions up to 521.

entry.title: Noise Modeling and Robust Detection for Yeast Pheromone Molecular Communication
entry.summary: Noise Characterization and Robust Signal Detection in Yeast Pheromone Molecular Communication arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies noise in a yeast-based molecular communication platform for cell-to-cell signaling, identifying gene transcription as the main noise source. The noise is modeled with a Markov birth-death process with Poisson arrivals and departures, and FUS1 gene expression is best described by a mixed Gaussian distribution. Maximum Likelihood Detection is evaluated by bit error rate for symbol-by-symbol and sequence transmission. Sequence detection yields lower error rates, at the cost of higher computational complexity.

entry.title: Computing fair item splits (EF1) with fewer value queries
entry.summary: Computing EF1 Allocations with Few Value Queries arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper presents a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that allocates m indivisible goods among n agents with nonnegative additive valuations. It uses O(n^5 log^2 m) value queries and guarantees envy-freeness up to one good (EF1). Compared with concurrent work, the algorithm and its proofs are much simpler, and the computation runs in polynomial time.

entry.title: Subsystem stabilizer (r,δ) locally recoverable codes: characterization, bounds, constructions
entry.summary: Subsystem Stabilizer (r,δ)-Locally Recoverable Codes: Characterization, Bounds and Constructions arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies locally recoverable subsystem stabilizer codes, where each coordinate lies in a repair set of size between δ and r+δ-1 that corrects up to δ-1 erasures while preserving the logical subsystem. It gives an algebraic characterization of local erasure recovery and applies it to CSS and Hermitian hull constructions. Redundancy, supported-subspace, and mixed counting bounds are derived, and for pure codes with overlapping repair sets, Singleton-type, alphabet-dependent, Griesmer, Hamming, and Plotkin bounds are established. Nine classes of pure codes are constructed from MDS stabilizer codes, Reed-Solomon codes, and linear codes with MDS Hermitian hulls.

entry.title: TAILROLL: Tail-Aware Rollout Acceleration for Reinforcement-Learning-Based LLM Post-Training
entry.summary: TAILROLL: Tail-Aware Rollout Acceleration for RL-Based LLM Post-Training arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes TAILROLL, an online scheduler that reduces idle compute during the rollout stage of reinforcement-learning post-training of large language models, where long-tail responses otherwise force engines to wait. It combines stateless in-flight request migration between engines at chunk boundaries with sufficiency-gated termination, which stops a response once its GRPO group has enough completed samples. Across ten configurations, the authors report reduced rollout bubble ratios, shorter rollout time in end-to-end training, and generation throughput gains of up to 33%.

entry.title: Polynomial-time decoding of quadratic and generalized quadratic residue codes up to half the square-root bound
entry.summary: A polynomial-time decoding algorithm up to half the square-root bound for quadratic residue and generalized quadratic residue codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies binary quadratic residue (QR) codes and their generalization, generalized quadratic residue (GQR) codes, whose minimum distance satisfies the square-root bound. The authors give a deterministic algorithm that, for every odd prime power q congruent to ±1 mod 8, corrects every error pattern of weight at most ⌊(√q−1)/2⌋ in the binary GQR code of length q. The algorithm runs in O(q^{9/2}) operations in F_q. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first polynomial-time decoder for GQR codes, correcting up to half the square-root bound, adapting Kopparty's character-value recovery tools with O(q^{9/2}) operations.

entry.title: Maximizing entropy of cube projections
entry.summary: Entropy maximization for cube projections arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proves that in every dimension n≥150, one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz for these dimensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that in dimensions n≥150 equal-magnitude directions maximize entropy of cube projections, resolving the Eskenazis–Nayar–Tkocz conjecture in those dimensions.

entry.title: Collecting cluster-wide measurements to analyze energy use in modern computing infrastructure
entry.summary: Collecting Infrastructure-Level Measures for Energy Analysis in Modern Computing Infrastructures arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper presents a scalable pipeline that gathers fine-grained measurements from multiple subsystems across a computing cluster, with consistent sampling and synchronized acquisition. The authors release a one-month dataset collected at 1 Hz from a research data center running HPC, Kubernetes services, and distributed storage. Two case studies, distributed I/O and large-language-model inference, show system-level dynamics that localized instrumentation misses.

entry.title: Fixed points and disequilibrium of negators for hyperbolic-valued probability distributions
entry.summary: Fixed-Point Results and Disequilibrium for Negators of Hyperbolic-Valued Probability Distributions arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the fixed-point structure of probability negators acting on hyperbolic-valued probability distributions and how disequilibrium changes along their iterates. Disequilibrium is defined as the separation between a distribution and the uniform distribution determined by its hyperbolic mass, using Euclidean, ℓ1, and Jensen–Shannon metrics. The authors establish hyperbolic Schur-convexity with sharp bounds and characterize the fixed-point sets of negators via an order-theoretic condition. Domination by Yager's negator gives explicit decay factors, and structural conditions are derived ensuring that disequilibrium converges to zero under repeated negation.

entry.title: From Apology to Action: How LLM Agents' Apologies, Compensation, and Cooperation Relate
entry.summary: From Apology to Action: Apologies, Compensation, and Cooperation in LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper uses Prisoner's Dilemma experiments to study whether apologies by four commercial large language model agents are linked to later cooperative behaviour. It also tests how access to one round of interaction history and offers of compensation alongside apologies affect outcomes. The findings show that verbal signals of conciliation do not always match the agents' subsequent actions.

entry.title: An Upper Bound on Non-Overlapping Codes
entry.summary: An upper bound on non-overlapping codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies binary non-overlapping codes, also called bifix-free or strong comma-free codes, which have been examined in information theory for over 60 years. It gives a self-contained proof that, as code length n grows, the number of codewords is bounded by (5/(6e)+O(n^{-1}))·2^n/n. This improves the previous best bound by Levenshtein (1970) by a factor of 5/6.

entry.title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: Two Parallel Research Traditions
entry.summary: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This survey compares two traditions in the mathematical theory of designing interaction rules for purposeful participants: mechanism design, with contract and implementation theory, and active systems theory, created by Burkov and developed into organizational control theory. It reviews main problems and results from 2006 to 2026, including robust and dynamic mechanism design, information design, market design, and algorithmic approaches. It also establishes correspondences between classical results of the two traditions and identifies where they diverge.

entry.title: Learning in-context adaptivity for LLMs via repeated game play
entry.summary: Learning In-Context Adaptivity for LLMs through Continual Gameplay arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper defines in-context adaptivity as an LLM agent's ability to improve decisions across episodes using experience stored in its context. The authors evaluate this in repeated imperfect-information games against unknown opponents, comparing agents with and without memory. They find memory gives little gain for open-weight models and inconsistent gains for frontier models, as agents record opponent tendencies but rarely change their play. They post-train Qwen3.5-9B with supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level reinforcement learning, which yields larger experience gains on unseen opponents.

entry.title: Axiomatic characterization of relative entropy
entry.summary: Axioms for relative entropy arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper characterizes positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences for normal states on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. A conditional-expectation identity can replace the two tensor assumptions. The proof relies on order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers, and an appendix establishes the needed analytic estimates using modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. A corresponding characterization is also obtained in the C*-algebraic setting. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors axiomatically characterize Araki relative entropy on arbitrary von Neumann algebras and extend the result to the C* setting.

entry.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness
entry.summary: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies a time-slotted status-update system in which samples are generated at will and sent over an erasure channel with success probability q. Average sampling and transmission rate constraints apply, and the sampler-transmitter pair decides whether to idle, retransmit, or replace a packet. The authors derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information and identify a stationary randomized policy with a 4-approximation guarantee.

entry.title: Lower bounds for computing graph degeneracy and k-cores in distributed networks
entry.summary: Lower Bounds for the Distributed Computation of Degeneracy and k-Core arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how many communication rounds are needed to compute the degeneracy and k-cores of a graph in distributed networks. Under the CONGEST model, the authors prove that approximating degeneracy within a factor of 2-ε requires Ω̃(√n) rounds, even in networks of diameter O(log n). They also give a conditional result, based on the circuit value problem, for deciding whether a graph is 2-degenerate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give lower bounds for distributed degeneracy and k-core computation, showing Ω̃(√n) rounds for 2-ε approximation in CONGEST and a conditional stronger bound.

entry.title: Knowledge Fermentation: a method that learns class variation shared across few-shot tasks
entry.summary: Knowledge Fermentation: Learning from Shared Variation in Few-Shot Classification arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes Knowledge Fermentation (KF), a few-shot classification method in which classes exchange what they know about within-class variation, recovering second-order knowledge that a handful of labeled examples cannot provide. Experiments on 14 datasets and 8 frozen encoders report performance on par with the best of six tuned inductive baselines. With unlabeled examples, the paper reports higher average one-shot accuracy and the best average among nine transductive methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose sharing within-class variation across classes, prove unbiasedness and non-expansion, and report one-shot accuracy rising from 52.4% to 65.8% across 14 datasets and 8 encoders.

entry.title: Bipartible Pattern: Routing HTTP Requests Over InfiniBand
entry.summary: The Bipartible Architecture Pattern: Transparently Directing HTTP Requests over InfiniBand arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes the Bipartible architecture pattern to speed up cloud-native workloads running on HPC systems. A copy of a global HTTP service (BPService) is placed on compute hosts, so HTTP storage requests are answered over InfiniBand instead of TCP/IP without changing the workload or network setup. The authors built a prototype for S3 and a hybrid version for a software repository service. They note that thorough read and write testing is required before production use.

entry.title: Sample complexity of channel coding: a new nonasymptotic framework
entry.summary: The Sample Complexity of Channel Coding arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces a framework for studying the fundamental limits of channel coding through nonasymptotic results. It defines a channel's sample complexity as the smallest blocklength at which information can be transmitted below a target error probability at a sufficient rate. For discrete memoryless channels, the authors derive explicit nonasymptotic bounds showing sample complexity is governed by the Augustin–Csiszár capacity of order 1/2 rather than ordinary capacity. The results are extended to the additive white Gaussian noise channel with a quadratic power constraint. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce channel coding sample complexity, show it is governed by the order-1/2 Augustin–Csiszár capacity, and give explicit nonasymptotic bounds.

entry.title: Polynomial-time algorithm for near-fair division of unwanted tasks
entry.summary: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies fairly dividing indivisible chores (tasks with negative value) among agents with additive disutilities, focusing on envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX) and its multiplicative approximations. The authors give an algorithm that computes a (3+ε)-EFX allocation in time polynomial in the input length and 1/ε, resolving an open question about polynomial-time computability. The result relies on a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for earning-restricted equilibria and a new procedure that converts approximate equilibria into (3+ε)-EFX-friendly allocations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open problem by giving a polynomial-time (3+ε)-EFX chore allocation algorithm, built on a new nonconvex program and an FPTAS for ER equilibria.

entry.title: GNoF: A GPU-native storage data path that reduces CPU and GPU core overhead for remote flash access
entry.summary: GNoF: A Low-SM-Overhead GPU-Native NVMe-over-Fabrics Completion Path for Data-Intensive GPU Workloads arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper addresses GPU workloads that read datasets stored on remote flash, where the host CPU traditionally handles every NVMe-over-Fabrics transaction, adding CPU load, synchronization, and redundant data copies. It presents GNoF, in which GPU threads build commands, ring doorbells, and process completions on the device, while the CPU handles only setup and administration.
