On a 200 Gb/s InfiniBand fabric, the authors report 1.77 million 4 KB IOPS per client with 0.37% host CPU use and about 1% SM occupancy, and compare it against three baselines.

entry.title: Optimal order-independent two-dimensional insdel Reed-Solomon codes built with cross-ratios
entry.summary: Optimal Ordering-Free Two-Dimensional Insdel Reed-Solomon Codes via Cross-Ratios arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies insertion-deletion (insdel) codes, which correct synchronization errors. It shows that for n≥6, any two-dimensional code meeting the half-Singleton bound is a Reed-Solomon code, requiring field size q≥C(n,3)+2. It further gives bounds on evaluation sets whose insdel distance does not depend on point ordering. Using cross-ratios, the authors construct such an ordering-free set of r+1 points in F_{r^3} for every prime power r, which is also robust against permutations combined with insdel errors.

entry.title: Recursive spectral graph partitioning for bit assignment in semantic communication
entry.summary: Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning Coding for Index Assignment in Semantic Communications arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper addresses how to map quantized semantic embeddings to binary codes so that bit-flip channel errors cause minimal reconstruction distortion in semantic communication. It proposes Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning (RSGP), which recursively splits the centroid affinity graph using the Fiedler eigenvector so early bits separate semantically distant groups. Experiments on Banking77 and MTEB show RSGP matches or exceeds the Binary Switching Algorithm's accuracy across codebook sizes and error profiles.

entry.title: Linear network coding for summing data across ring networks
entry.summary: Linear Network Coding for Sum All-Reduce over Ring Networks arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies Sum All-Reduce, a collective operation in which every node on a directed ring obtains the componentwise sum of all nodes' vectors. The authors analyze the problem using linear network coding, which includes reduce-multicast as a special case, and give a necessary and sufficient feasibility condition based on the coding matrices. They prove a lower bound on the number of time units needed for a ring of N nodes with unit-capacity links, and show the bound is tight over every field, with explicit codes achieving it.

entry.title: Stage Splitting: Energy and Latency Trade-offs in Multimodal LLM Serving
entry.summary: A Matter of Stages: Energy-Latency Trade-offs in Multimodal LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper examines energy and latency trade-offs when serving multimodal large language models online, comparing fused serving with EPD disaggregation that places visual encoding, prefill, and decode on separate GPUs under a fixed three-GPU budget. Across 18 workload combinations, the authors also test single-stage and uniform frequency reduction. Disaggregation lowers GPU energy per successful request by 13.3-37.0% but raises mean TTFT, while uniform downclocking to 80% cuts energy by 11.7-18.6%. Based on these findings, the authors propose a budgeted frequency exploration strategy for selecting energy-efficient configurations under latency constraints.

entry.title: Exact optimal delivery for cyclically L-separated placement in multi-access coded caching
entry.summary: The Exact Optimal Delivery Scheme for the Cyclically L-Separated Placement in Multi-Access Coded Caching arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies the multi-access coded caching system proposed by Hachem et al., where users access consecutive cache nodes in a cyclic topology. For cyclically L-separated placement, the authors derive a new converse bound and propose a determinant-based interference alignment scheme that achieves this bound exactly. They also give a general converse bound for arbitrary uncoded placements and show that the scheme's load is within a factor of two of the global bound under uncoded placement.

entry.title: Designing Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes Resistant to Pulsed Jamming in Space Telemetry
entry.summary: Analysis and Design of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes for Pulsed-Jamming-Resilient Space Telemetry arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper addresses jamming threats to space telemetry downlinks by proposing an analysis and design framework for protograph-based spatially coupled LDPC codes. It derives a two-state EXIT recursion that tracks clean and jammed symbols separately, and studies non-interleaved pulsed jamming under random lifting. The codes are optimized with a constrained differential-evolution search. Under random pulse positions with jamming state information, the designed ensembles, decoded by sliding window decoding, reach a bit error rate of 10^-4 at lower signal-to-noise ratios than the benchmark codes.

entry.title: Nearly Settling the Complexity of Connected ε-Envy-Free Cake Cutting
entry.summary: Nearly Settling the Complexity of Connected ǎrepsilon-Envy-Free Cake Cutting arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies fair cake cutting, seeking connected ε-envy-free allocations using Robertson-Webb queries as the measure of query complexity. It shows that polylogarithmic queries suffice for up to five agents, while seven or more agents require polynomial-in-1/ε queries even with additive valuations, leaving six agents unresolved. The paper also analyzes computational complexity, finding polynomial-time solvability for five agents under certain valuation models and UEOPL- and PPAD-hardness results for larger numbers of agents. ★★★★ Notable: The authors settle the five-agent query complexity case, giving polylogarithmic upper bounds and polynomial lower bounds for seven or more agents, plus computational hardness results.

entry.title: How Carbon Intensity Data Source Choice Affects Carbon-Aware Resource Management
entry.summary: Investigating the Impact of CI-Source Sensitivity in Carbon-Aware Resource Management Systems arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies how differences between carbon intensity (CI) data sources affect placement decisions and operational outcomes in carbon-aware resource management systems. The authors compare CI data from Wattnet and ElectricityMaps across five Central European zones. They propose the ESCAPE framework, which tests source switching and controlled perturbations using CarbonEdge. Switching CI sources changed the dominant placement site in 43.50% of cases and altered reported operational outcomes.

entry.title: Designing neural networks that fit the physical network they run on
entry.summary: Network-Native DNN Architecture Synthesis for Distributed Inference arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper reverses the usual approach to distributed deep neural network inference by letting the physical network's topology define the dependencies between nodes, rather than partitioning a predefined model onto the network. Neural computation is allocated across nodes under communication, computation, storage, synchronization, and latency constraints. The authors introduce LPAS, a linear programming-based synthesis algorithm, which reports relative gaps below 0.6% to the LP upper bound and higher classification accuracy after training than the model-first baseline.

entry.title: A recursive method for building perfect quaternion arrays of any power-of-two shape
entry.summary: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape 2^a₁×cdots×2^a_d over the Unit Quaternions arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper extends Blake's recursive construction of perfect sequences over the unit quaternions to arrays of any dimension. Operations applied one direction at a time produce perfect arrays of shapes 2^a × M_2 × ... × M_d. In contrast, perfect binary arrays of such shapes exist only under a restriction from a theorem of Jedwab and Kraemer, while the quaternion construction imposes no restriction on shape. The paper also shows that single arrays with a non-central twist exist in two dimensions.

entry.title: Top-Level Operational Equilibrium: Can a Distributed System's Response Be Predicted from Its Own Telemetry?
entry.summary: Top-Level Operational Equilibrium: When is the response of a distributed system predictable from its own telemetry? arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper defines top-level operational equilibrium (TLOE), a condition under which a running distributed system's response to a control change can be predicted from its passive telemetry. TLOE requires stationarity with time-scale separation, sufficiency of a top-level aggregate for the controls, and time-reversibility of that aggregate. The authors prove that such an aggregate exists if and only if the minimal sufficient statistic of the controls is time-reversible, and they test the conditions on reference models. Validation on real telemetry is left to future work.

entry.title: A combinatorial test for when traffic-style games avoid the strong Braess paradox
entry.summary: A Combinatorial Characterization of Immunity to the Strong Braess Paradox arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies the strong Braess paradox in nonatomic congestion games, where cutting resource costs or demands raises at least one group's equilibrium cost. It gives a combinatorial characterization of when a system of strategies is immune to this paradox, using series-parallel matroid conditions, and resolves an open question posed by Fujishige et al. (2017). The authors also show that whenever immunity fails, a paradox can be constructed with unit demands and affine costs, and that nonimmunity has polynomial-size certificates when strategies are listed explicitly. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question of Fujishige et al. with a matroid-based combinatorial characterization of immunity to strong Braess paradox.

entry.title: L-systems on the Large Witt Design
entry.summary: L-systems on the large Witt design arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies the maximum size m(n,24,L) of a family of 24-element subsets of an n-element set whose distinct members intersect in sizes from L={0,1,2,3,4,8}, a set tied to the large Witt design S(5,8,24). The authors prove that positive constants c, C and n0 exist such that cn^(316/63) ≤ m(n,24,L) ≤ Cn^(169/29) for all n ≥ n0. Similar results are obtained for systems associated with S(4,7,23), S(3,6,22) and S(3,4,14).

entry.title: Weighted sum-rate optimization for near-field STAR-RIS ISAC systems with hardware impairments
entry.summary: Weighted Sum-Rate Optimization of Near-Field STAR-RIS-Aided ISAC Systems Under Hardware Impairments arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies maximizing weighted sum-rate in a multi-user MIMO integrated sensing and communication system assisted by a STAR-RIS under the energy splitting protocol. The base station to STAR-RIS link uses far-field propagation, while STAR-RIS to user links use near-field spherical wavefronts, and hardware impairments such as phase perturbations and signal-dependent distortion are included. An alternating optimization and successive convex approximation approach is used to solve the active and passive beamforming subproblems. Numerical results show stable convergence and higher weighted sum-rate than direct-link transmission, with severe hardware impairments causing saturation at high transmit power.

entry.title: Payoff-based conditions certifying convergence to pure Nash equilibria under replicator dynamics
entry.summary: Payoff-Based Certificates for Convergence to Pure Nash Equilibria under Replicator Dynamics arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper studies finite bimatrix games and gives a payoff-based sufficient condition, E>0, under which an interior starting state converges to a specified strict pure Nash equilibrium under replicator dynamics. The construction combines growth-rate bounds on log probability ratios with a first integral of a two-dimensional comparison system. It also provides a finite exact test for rational inputs, closed-form box probabilities and convergence-time bounds, and extensions to multiplayer games and discrete-time exponential-weights learning.

entry.title: Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition
entry.summary: Beyond Service Discovery: Coverage Awareness in LLM-Driven Service Composition arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper distinguishes reuse discovery, finding relevant published assets, from reuse coverage, whether those assets support the transformations a request needs. It evaluates PipeFinder, an LLM-driven framework, on 99 consumer requests against a fixed catalogue. Relevant data products were found reliably, but successful composition was much harder, and when required services were missing the system usually built a pipeline anyway. Explicitly adding coverage checks to planning substantially improved recognition of unsatisfiable requests.

entry.title: Functional Information and Optimal Limits for Channel Simulation and Lossy Coding
entry.summary: Functional Information, Optimal Channel Simulation and Lossy Source Coding arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies the minimum achievable rates of one-shot coding problems, such as channel simulation and lossy source coding, to within a constant number of bits. It introduces a new information measure, the functional information I_F(X→Y), which characterizes the minimum rate of channel simulation with common randomness to within 1.45 bits. The authors use this result to define a functional rate-distortion function and bound the one-shot operational rate-distortion function, and they extend the framework to a Rényi-type functional information. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce functional information and characterize one-shot channel simulation rate within 1.45 bits, extending to lossy source coding and Rényi variants.

entry.title: Achievable information rate of faster-than-Nyquist signaling with a reduced-complexity BCJR receiver
entry.summary: Achievable Information Rate for FTN under a Reduced Complexity BCJR Receiver arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies the achievable information rate (AIR) of faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling with finite constellations, using full-state and reduced-state BCJR receivers with bidirectional decision feedback. The detection problem is formulated in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and detection errors are characterized by distances between competing sequences. The authors also derive an outage criterion for reduced-state detection, where the AIR is zero. The results show that reduced-state detection can suffer outage even at high signal-to-noise ratio due to residual inter-symbol interference.

entry.title: Ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes, combining NRT and sum-rank metrics
entry.summary: The ordered sum-rank metric and linearized multiplicity codes: NRT meets sum-rank arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper introduces linearized multiplicity codes, generalizing both linearized Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes. It also defines the ordered sum-rank metric, which generalizes the sum-rank metric and the NRT (ordered Hamming) metric. A Singleton bound is established for this metric, and linearized multiplicity codes are shown to attain it, making them maximum ordered sum-rank distance codes.

entry.title: Two-Robot Evacuation from a Unit Disk Under Segment Visibility
entry.summary: Two-Robot Evacuation from a Unit Disk in the Segment Visibility Model arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper studies two unit-speed robots starting at the center of a unit disk that must both reach an exit at an unknown boundary point. Under segment visibility, a target is discovered once it lies on the segment joining the robots, even if they have not reached it, and robots may leave the disk while searching. The authors give a three-phase tangent-and-arc algorithm with exact worst-case evacuation time 2√3+π/3 ≈ 4.511299. They also prove a matching lower bound for descending horizontal full-slice sweeps, and the optimal time over all segment-visibility algorithms remains open.

entry.title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays for Cell-Free MIMO: Joint Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation Design
entry.summary: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (SRAs) for Cell-Free MIMO: Network-Wide Design of Antenna Activation and Panel Orientation arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies a cell-free multiuser MIMO system using sparse rotatable arrays, where distributed access points select active antennas and adjust panel orientations under a network-wide activation budget. It formulates a two-timescale stochastic optimization that sets antenna activation and panel orientations on long timescales and precoders on short timescales. The authors develop an alternating algorithm combining sample-average approximation, WMMSE, and greedy search. Numerical results show the design outperforms a fixed-array benchmark with fewer active antennas.

entry.title: Error-correcting codes without parity-check bits: boosting symbol dependence to cut channel errors
entry.summary: Error-correcting codes without parity-check bits arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper proposes a new approach to error correction in communication channels. The input sequence is transformed before transmission so that dependencies between symbols increase substantially, and this property is then used to correct errors after transmission. A natural application is binary sequences with per-symbol entropy below one, where the sequence length stays constant through encoding and decoding. The authors develop a maximum likelihood decoding algorithm with linear encoding and decoding time and test it experimentally on popular channel models, finding parameter sets for which the method is quite effective.

entry.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattice theta series
entry.summary: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The Gaussian mass of a lattice is its theta series evaluated at a real nome, relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The paper proves inequalities comparing the Gaussian mass of lattices to that of the integer lattice, covering lattices built from binary, quaternary and senary self-dual codes and extremal unimodular lattices of both types. It also gives an averaging bound over the genus of Type II lattices and extends the binary Construction A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus.

entry.title: Exact Redundancy Under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Limits
entry.summary: Exact Redundancy under Average and Almost-Sure Distortion Constraints arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper characterizes the exact redundancy of lossy source coding under average and almost-sure distortion constraints. For general source and output alphabets, it establishes asymptotic redundancy coefficients under suitable regularity conditions. Under average distortion, the coefficient is half the minimum probability that an output reveals source information among rate-distortion optimal channels; under almost-sure distortion, it is either 1/2 or 1 depending on whether the D-tilted information is constant. Both converses follow from a common change-of-measure inequality, and the required conditions are shown to always hold for finite alphabets.

entry.title: IA-MoE: An Intensity-Aware Mixture of Experts for Efficient Split Inference of Neural Networks
entry.summary: IA-MoE: An Intensity-Aware Mixture of Experts for DNN Inference arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper proposes IA-MoE, a Mixture of Experts framework for running deep neural network inference across edge and cloud servers. It models model partitioning as a bilateral matching between layer tasks and virtual machine resources for each request, dynamically splitting DNNs to jointly reduce end-to-end latency and energy use. Evaluated with AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 on two public datasets in an enhanced CloudSimSDN simulator, IA-MoE reportedly outperforms baseline methods on weighted normalized latency and energy metrics.

entry.title: A recursive method for building perfect and odd perfect sequences of any length over unit quaternions
entry.summary: A Recursive Construction of Perfect and Odd Perfect Sequences of Unbounded Length over the Unit Quaternions arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper gives a recursive construction, with closed-form index functions, of perfect and odd perfect periodic autocorrelation sequences over the unit quaternions in every length 2^n. The construction uses twisted periodic extensions and shows that a single sequence of length not divisible by 4 cannot carry the needed twist, while complementary pairs called i-pairs can. Explicit index formulas for i-pairs are given, along with the lengths of the odd perfect and perfect sequences derived from them.

entry.title: Boomerang spectrum of a nonlinear power function over a finite field
entry.summary: On the boomerang spectrum of the APN power function x^q+2 over F_q² arXiv · Nov 15, 2026This paper studies the boomerang spectrum of the almost perfect nonlinear power function x^{q+2} over F_{q^2}, where q is an odd prime power with q≡1 (mod 6). Using a connection between boomerang and (-1)-differential entries, the problem is reduced to counting roots of one equation. The authors determine the full contribution from nonzero parameters in F_q and give a quintic over F_q for parameters outside F_q.

entry.title: Keeping In-Network Computation Going in Satellite Networks: A Semantic Continuity Architecture
entry.summary: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity arXiv · Nov 15, 2026The paper argues that computations on satellites often outlast the paths and providers that first served them, and proposes organizing in-network computing around one continuing logical computation. It presents an architecture that separates logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, illustrated with a wildfire assessment example. In a 300-node Linux prototype, stage-wise placement met deadlines for 82.08% of positions across 120 images, compared with 76.06% for single-node placement.

entry.title: Proportional veto fairness in multiwinner elections with ranked ballots
entry.summary: Veto Proportionality in Multiwinner Voting with Ranked Preferences arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies veto proportionality in committee elections where voters submit ranked preferences. It introduces the proportional multiwinner veto core (PMVC), which extends Moulin's singlewinner veto core by letting voter groups partially veto sets of candidates. The authors analyze how the PMVC relates to existing fairness notions and design voting rules guaranteed to select committees from the PMVC.

entry.title: Rival Market Makers' Spreads Do Not Widen When a Competitor Gets Better Information
entry.summary: Spreads Don't Price a Rival Market Maker's Information arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper asks whether uninformed market makers widen their bid-ask spreads when a competitor receives a more precise private signal about a persistent state driving order flow. The authors model this as a stochastic quoting game, learn strategies with independent reinforcement learning, and benchmark against an exact dynamic-programming solution for the single-agent case. Across all configurations studied, the uninformed makers' average spread does not increase with the rival's precision; it is unchanged where competition is weak and tightens where competition is strong.

entry.title: Entropy- and quadratic-based metrics for scheduling LDPC belief-propagation decoding
entry.summary: Entropy-Based and Quadratic Conditional Innovation Metrics for Informed Dynamic Scheduling of Belief-Propagation Decoding for LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes two improved conditional innovation (CI) metrics, E-CI and Q-CI, to guide informed dynamic scheduling in belief-propagation decoding of LDPC codes. Both metrics separate each posterior probability into a decision side and a reliability-related distance term, which is replaced by an entropy-based quantity in E-CI and approximated by its leading quadratic term in Q-CI. Numerical results indicate that the proposed metrics generally achieve lower frame error rates than the original CI metric, with advantages depending on the code and decoding procedure.

entry.title: Zero-shot diffusion image compression using sectioned codebooks and a single channel code
entry.summary: Zero-shot diffusion image compression with sectioned codebooks and one channel code arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes sectioned codebooks for zero-shot diffusion image codecs such as Turbo-DDCM, which compress images without training. Each coding step is split into sections, each with its own large codebook, and the best vector is sent as a short bit field. At equal bits, the method raises PSNR by 0.18 to 0.51 dB on three datasets and saves 16 to 21% of bits at equal PSNR. Compared with a codec protected by one BCH channel code at equal total bits, it outperforms reported robust codecs on two datasets, by up to 7.74 dB at the highest bit error rate.

entry.title: New optimal rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams
entry.summary: New constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for quasi-block monotone Ferrers diagrams arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, which are used in constructing constant dimension subspace codes for random network coding. Using the multiplicative property of the kernel filtration of a nilpotent map, the authors construct optimal codes for block monotone diagrams. By puncturing and shortening on columns, they extend these results to block strictly monotone and quasi-block strictly monotone diagrams.

entry.title: Accuracy Guarantees for Fixed-Point Emulation of Matrix Multiplication
entry.summary: Providing Accuracy Guarantees for the Fixed-Point Emulation of Matrix Multiplication arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies emulating double-precision matrix multiplication on fast low-precision hardware using fixed-point methods such as Ozaki-II, with software that chooses the mantissa bit count automatically. The authors analyze worst-case and average-case errors of fixed-point and floating-point dot products and define exponent span capacities that set the extra mantissa bits an input needs. They prove that 53 bits plus such a capacity and a small constant preserve the classical worst-case error bound for a floating-point dot product, and demonstrate this in software.

entry.title: Rank functions of flag matroids and their use in order-neutral submodular valuations
entry.summary: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper gives a rank function axiomatization of flag matroids, defined as sequences of matroid quotients, and shows it is cryptomorphic to that definition. It links flag matroid rank functions to order-neutral submodular valuations from computational economics, showing they coincide for length-k flag matroids. The authors prove every order-neutral submodular valuation is a gross-substitute valuation, but not every one is a Rado valuation.

entry.title: NVFP4-MLA: Unified FP4 Storage and Computation for Attention Cache in Large Models
entry.summary: NVFP4-MLA: Unified FP4 KV-Cache Storage and Attention Computation for Multi-Head Latent Attention arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper introduces NVFP4-MLA, the first design that uses FP4 precision for both key-value cache storage and attention computation in multi-head latent attention. It combines a quantization method that adds residuals only to sensitive channels with two-dimensional quantization blocks that avoid requantization between the two attention matrix multiplications. On DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-K3, it matches BF16 MLA average accuracy across nine benchmarks while compressing the MLA KV cache by 3.20x and 3.05x. On NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, the attention kernel runs up to 2.82x faster than FP8 MLA on DeepSeek-R1 and up to 2.71x faster on Kimi-K3.

entry.title: Minimum field extension degrees needed for exact Reed-Solomon code repair at the cut-set bound
entry.summary: Minimum Extension Degrees for Reed-Solomon Codes:Exact Values and a Quadratic Transition arXiv · Oct 26, 2026The paper studies how large a field extension a Reed-Solomon code needs so that every lost node can be exactly repaired from any chosen set of d helpers, at the cut-set bound. For 3≤k<d<n≤2d-2, the authors prove the minimum extension degree over any prime power field is exactly sQ_s(n), where s=d-k+1. They also show that any nonlinear repair scheme reaching the cut-set bound induces an F_p-linear scheme, so the prime-field lower bounds hold without assuming linearity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine exact minimum extension degrees for Reed-Solomon repair at the cut-set bound for 3≤k<d<n≤2d-2 and report that nonlinear repair reduces to linear repair.

entry.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy field
entry.summary: Self-organizing recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper proposes a collective foraging model in which an agent that finds a resource recruits others through a linear-threshold cascade, and its movement rewires the communication network, producing a self-limiting cycle of aggregation and release. The authors report that recruitment to discoveries, marginal-value patch leaving, and Lévy search with local exploitation emerge together without tuning. Gains reach up to 7.6 times the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered.

entry.title: Go under Chinese rules with succinct game history is EXPSPACE-complete
entry.summary: Go under Chinese Rules with a Succinct Game History is Complete for Exponential Space arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of Go under Chinese rules, which include a no-repetition (super-ko) rule. The authors introduce a succinct game history, a Boolean circuit that determines whether a board position already occurred in the game. They prove that deciding whether Black has a winning strategy under this representation is EXPSPACE-complete. The starting position in the hardness proof can be reached by legal play. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce succinct game histories and report EXPSPACE-completeness of Go under Chinese rules with no-repetition, resolving a long-open question.

entry.title: Zero-SM NCCL: A guide to GPU communication that avoids using streaming multiprocessors
entry.summary: Zero-SM NCCL: A Systematic Guide to Designing and Deploying SM-Free GPU Communication arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents Zero-SM NCCL, a GPU communication approach that launches no SM kernels, instead using CUDA stream memory operations, copy engines, and a stream-ordered CPU proxy for RDMA. On GB200 NVL72 and B200 NVL8 systems, it reaches up to 1.36x higher AllGather bandwidth and reduces median GEMM overlap slowdown from 33% to 4%. The authors find it helps large transfers and deep pipelines but hurts small messages and host-bound workloads, and distill these results into deployment guidelines.</summary> ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present SM-free GPU communication using copy engines and a CPU proxy, reporting measurements on GB200/B200 for AllGather and overlapped GEMMs plus Megatron-LM training results.

entry.title: Using Factory Load Valleys to Host Distributed AI Servers with Less Grid Connection
entry.summary: Coordinating Distributed AI Servers with Industrial Loads to Reduce Grid-Interconnection Needs arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper proposes placing distributed AI servers at factories during production valleys and coordinating AI workloads with industrial loads. The authors formulate a joint optimization that sizes CPU and GPU servers, schedules deadline-constrained tasks, and routes tasks among factories, and compare it with new large data centers across 31 Chinese manufacturing industries. They report that AI servers placed at factories need substantially less additional grid interconnection capacity than new large data centers.

entry.title: A unified method for jointly estimating channels, detecting data, and tracking phase noise in massive MIMO
entry.summary: Joint Channel Estimation, Data Detection, and Phase Noise Tracking in Massive MIMO Systems arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper addresses uplink massive MIMO systems, where phase noise from imperfect oscillators degrades communication and grows worse at higher carrier frequencies. It proposes a unified framework that tracks the evolving phase noise consistently across pilot and data transmission while jointly estimating the channel and detecting data. The framework has three parts: VB-Tracking for channel estimation and phase noise tracking during pilots, VB-Detecting for joint data detection and phase tracking, and VB-Refining for periodically re-estimating the channel during data transmission. Simulations show lower channel NMSE and symbol error rate than the baselines, with the advantage widening at high SNR and under severe phase noise.

entry.title: Surrogate Symbols in Wireless Communications: Using Phase Optimization to Turn Co-Channel Interference into Usable Signal
entry.summary: Surrogate Symbols in Wireless Communications arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper addresses co-channel interference (CCI) in a network of single-antenna transmitters and receivers that reuse the same channel. It proposes a discrete phase-optimization framework called "Game of Phases: Surrogate Symbol Optimization" with two algorithms, MiPIP and MaPRIS. The authors argue that MaPRIS can make the interference approximate a desired symbol even when a receiver's own desired link is zero, and report that simulations confirm these findings.

entry.title: Full Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function
entry.summary: The Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies APN functions induced by monomials over finite fields, which resist differential attacks when used in block ciphers. The authors determine the complete Walsh spectrum, and thus the linearity, of the Dobbertin APN monomial, answering a problem open for over 20 years. Using known connections, the result also gives the asymptotically largest Sidon sets constructed so far in elementary abelian 2-groups and nearly optimal binary linear codes with minimum distance 5.

entry.title: Proof of a conjecture on maximizing entropy for cube projections
entry.summary: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper completes the Eskenazis–Nayar–Tkocz conjecture, which states that for one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is largest in directions where all coordinates have equal magnitude. Pang had already proved the conjecture for dimensions at least 150, and this work covers the remaining dimensions. The proof combines polynomial entropy bounds, exact certificates, and certified one-dimensional integration, and the paper also gives quantitative stability estimates with source code and verification outputs.

entry.title: Stochastic games where entropy of a probability distribution is the payoff
entry.summary: Stochastic Games with Distributional Entropy Objectives arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper introduces two-player zero-sum stochastic games whose configurations are probability distributions over the states of a finite arena and whose stage reward is Shannon entropy. MIN tries to concentrate the distribution while MAX tries to disperse it. Because entropy is nonlinear, the paper formalises three semantics depending on whether randomness is averaged or sampled before entropy is evaluated, and analyses their determinacy, optimal strategies, and computational complexity.

entry.title: Voting Rights Lost in Spatial Voting Games
entry.summary: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper studies a self-referential problem in which group members decide who may join the group, as with voting rights and membership rules. The authors introduce franchise elections, where voting members vote to change the electorate. They show that in a two-dimensional ideological space these elections can produce complex behavior for any social choice function. Using the Yolk social choice function, they show that franchise elections can cycle with any period.

entry.title: BPU-SpikeMM: Exact Matrix Multiplication via Spike Encoding on Neuromorphic Chips
entry.summary: BPU-SpikeMM:Exact Matrix Multiplication via Spatio-Temporal Spike Encoding on Real Neuromorphic Hardware arXiv · Nov 14, 2026This paper presents BPU-SpikeMM, a framework that performs matrix multiplication on real neuromorphic hardware (BPU) using spatio-temporal spike encoding. The authors prove exact equivalence of spike-encoded matrix multiplication under the BPU execution paradigm and distinguish it from mathematical equivalence. They build an offloading pipeline supporting multiple encoding schemes and evaluate them on correctness, temporal and spatial resource cost, and event-driven metrics. Results confirm direct-readout equivalence across all evaluated encodings, with applicability depending on trade-offs among these costs.

entry.title: New Results on the Subfield Metric: Advances in Error-Correcting Code Theory
entry.summary: New Results on the Subfield Metric arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper further develops the recently introduced λ-subfield metric, studying extremal codes, classical bounds and asymptotic densities. It examines Maximum λ-subfield Distance (MλD) codes that attain a Singleton-type bound, establishing structural restrictions on their parameters and extending the theory to sublinear codes. The asymptotic density of MλD codes is compared with that of MDS and MRD codes across several parameter regimes. The paper also addresses Plotkin-type bounds, Griesmer-, Elias- and Johnson-type bounds.

entry.title: Movable-antenna-aided integrated sensing and communication under time- and frequency-division protocols
entry.summary: Movable Antenna-Aided ISAC: A Time- and Frequency-Division Framework arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enhanced by movable antennas under time division duplex and frequency division duplex protocols, where sensing and communication use orthogonal time or frequency resources. It derives a wideband target-position Cramér-Rao bound for a pulse radar with pulse compression, covering delay and angle estimation errors. For multiuser downlink communication, it jointly optimizes antenna position vectors and resource allocation to maximize the minimum user rate under a sensing requirement. Numerical results show that antenna position optimization enlarges the communication-sensing tradeoff region, with TDD and FDD favoring different configurations.

entry.title: Extending the linear dynamic range of Rydberg atomic receivers via band-limited reconstruction
entry.summary: Linear Dynamic Range Extension for Rydberg Atomic Receiver via Band-Limited Reconstruction arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper addresses nonlinear distortion in Rydberg-atom radio-frequency receivers that occurs at high input signal levels due to their limited linear dynamic range. The authors analyze the distortion mechanisms and propose a physics-informed band-limited iterative reconstruction (PI-BLIR) method. It reconstructs the distorted signal by solving a constrained maximum-likelihood problem with gradient descent, using only digital post-processing. Simulations show the method extends the linear dynamic range by more than 14 dB and improves demodulation performance.

entry.title: Upper bounds on codes that correct and detect errors together
entry.summary: Hamming and Johnson-Type Bounds for Joint Error Correction and Detection arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper derives upper bounds on the size of codes over q-ary Hamming spaces that jointly correct errors of weight up to c and detect errors of weight between c+1 and c+c'. It gives a joint bound that reduces to the Hamming bound when c'=0, introduces joint perfect codes, and shows binary repetition codes attain the bound when n=2c+c'+1. A Johnson-type extension further strictly improves the bound for certain binary codes.

entry.title: Optimal-rate streaming codes for three-node relay networks with extended delay
entry.summary: Rate Optimal Streaming Codes Under an Extended Delay Profile for Three-Node Relay Networks arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies streaming codes for a three-node relay network with burst lengths and an end-to-end decoding delay. It proposes two binary constructions, SR and SR-2, which let the relay forward causally invertible combinations of current and past source symbols. Under stated conditions, these constructions reach the non-adaptive rate upper bound, with SR-2 covering a wider range. The paper also proves two limitations of systematic ordinary coordinate forwarding regarding when the rate upper bound can be attained.

entry.title: Multi-GPU versions of a parallel method for solving tridiagonal equation systems
entry.summary: Multi-GPU Tridiagonal Partition Algorithm arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents multi-GPU and multi-GPU recursive versions of the parallel partition method for solving linear equation systems with tridiagonal coefficient matrices. The authors implement these methods in CUDA. They run computational experiments on one and two GPU cards across different system sizes and numbers of recursive steps, and analyze the results.

entry.title: Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
entry.summary: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies the classical self-stabilizing Δ+1 coloring algorithm, where vertices are activated at random one at a time. It treats the number of color changes as a random variable and analyzes its mean, variance, and exact distribution on several graph families. The mean depends on the degree distribution, the variance requires information at distance two including triangles, and the full distribution needs the whole graph.

entry.title: Ranking wireless nodes in a line using Fourier-based maximum-likelihood estimation
entry.summary: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version) arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper applies non-abelian Fourier theory to maximum-likelihood estimation of node order in a line topology, using signal strength measurements affected only by shadowing. For uncorrelated shadowing, the authors report up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods. For correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance, recovery is exact and independent of shadowing variance, a result the implementation confirms for σ/α up to 7.0. The key is the covariance's null space, whose dimension depends on the topology and whose orientation depends on the correlation function only through per-link variances.

entry.title: OrbitWeaver: LLM Agent Planning with Simulation Feedback for Orbital GPU Clusters Linked by Optical Links
entry.summary: OrbitWeaver: LLM Agent Planning with Simulation Feedback for Optically Interconnected Orbital GPU Clusters arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents OrbitWeaver, an offline large language model agent planner that jointly optimizes GPU rank placement and communication order in orbital GPU clusters connected by optical inter-satellite links. Using communication structure, execution dependencies, and simulation feedback, it builds and refines plans that reduce link contention and dependency blocking. In simulations, it reduces aggregate mean job completion time by 6.2% to 33.5% compared with the baselines CASSINI, Crux, and Symphony.

entry.title: SIMTurn: Lightweight Scheduling of Divergent Thread Groups to Prevent Deadlock in GPU Warps
entry.summary: SIMTurn: Lightweight Divergent Subgroup Scheduling for Intra-Warp Synchronization arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents SIMTurn, a lightweight mechanism combining compiler and hardware support to let divergent thread subgroups within a GPU warp make forward progress while keeping stack-based reconvergence. The compiler inserts a yield instruction at potentially blocking loops, and a bounded pool of resumable subgroups lets a waiting subgroup hand execution to a sibling that can advance. Implemented on the open-source Vortex GPGPU, SIMTurn adds 17-24% scheduler-area overhead relative to IPDOM, versus 39-91% for per-thread ITS. On kernels with cross-subgroup parallelism it tracks ITS closely and reaches up to 2.7x the speed of a software-serialized IPDOM baseline.

entry.title: TailGuard-GDS: Tail-Latency-Aware Control of GPU Storage Data Transfers
entry.summary: TailGuard-GDS: Tail-Safe Control of GPU Storage Data Movement arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents TailGuard-GDS, a runtime that chooses, for each application phase, among semantically equivalent ways of moving data between NVMe storage and GPU memory. It profiles candidate plans and minimizes GPU-visible tail latency under phase constraints, revisiting decisions as conditions change. Integrated with PyTorch FSDP and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, it reduces FSDP step p95 by 18.4% and GPU-idle p95 by 25.3% compared with the strongest fixed path.

entry.title: Minimal Information Inequalities for Regenerating Codes via Algebra
entry.summary: Toward the Minimal Set of Information Inequalities in Regenerating Codes: An Algebraic Approach arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies information-theoretic outer bounds for exact-repair regenerating codes, which can be written as linear programs but whose Shannon-type systems contain many implicit equalities and redundant inequalities. The authors specify a reduced system for the (n,n-1,n-1) exact-repair model using the closure structure induced by repair dependencies, and prove it is equivalent to the original system. They provide an algorithm that constructs this system for any n, counts its entropy coordinates, and bounds its number of inequalities. For every n≥2, they show the reduced system has no implicit equalities and that each distinct defining inequality is nonredundant and defines a facet.

entry.title: Proof that no quasi-symmetric 2-(33,15,35) design exists
entry.summary: Nonexistence of a quasi-symmetric 2-(33,15,35) design arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper shows that no quasi-symmetric 2-(33,15,35) design exists with intersection numbers 6 and 9. The proof examines the ternary code generated by the incidence vectors of the blocks, together with its dual code.

entry.title: INC-SRv6: Using Segment Routing Headers for In-Network Route Discovery and Fast Failover in Dynamic Drone Networks
entry.summary: INC-SRv6: In-Network Route Exploration and Fast Failover Using Segment Routing Headers in Dynamic UAV Networks arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents INC-SRv6, an in-network routing method that repurposes the IPv6 Segment Routing Header and its Segments Left pointer into a self-learning, fast-failover distributed control plane. In simulations of 200-node 3D UAV networks with high-speed flight and repeated relay outages, it improves packet delivery over reactive routing. It also greatly reduces 95th-percentile tail delay and the number of control packets.

entry.title: Correlation distribution for a Niho exponent class via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums
entry.summary: Correlation distribution for a class of Niho exponents via self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and Kloosterman sums arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies the correlation distribution between a binary m-sequence of period q²−1 and its d-decimation, where q=2^m with even m≥6 and d=s(q−1)+1 with 4s≡5 (mod q+1). The cross-correlation function takes seven values q(i−1)−1 for 0≤i≤6. The frequencies of these values are determined through low-degree self-conjugate-reciprocal polynomials and three mixed Kloosterman sums.
